newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila changes mind, allows in two South Africans.
newsitem.headline: Manila changes mind, allows in two South Africans.

text.p: Philippine immigration officials on Tuesday admitted two South African unionists invited to an "anti-imperialist" meeting in Manila coinciding with the APEC summit after initially barring their entry and holding them for six hours.
The immigration bureau released the pair after organisers of the "Anti-Imperialist World Peasant Summit" interceded for them and said they were delegates to the meeting which starts on November 10.
Luanda Makupula and Baca Tembinkosi were kept at an airport office and later at the bureau of immigration in central Manila before their release.
"We told them there was no legal reason to keep them out," a spokesman for the organisers, the leftist Farmers' Movement of the Philippines (KMP) said.
KMP said the two were from the South African Agricultural Plantation Workers' Union, affiliated to President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress.
Philippine officials are determined to prevent any threat to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit on November 25, to be attended by U.S. President Bill Clinton and regional leaders.
Immigration official Danilo Perez told reporters after the two South Africans arrived: "We are making arrangements to deport (them) immediately due to their doubtful intentions."
Immigration authorities earlier refused an entry visa to 1996 Nobel Peace Prize co-winner and East Timorese activist Jose Ramos-Horta and have pledged to keep out any potential foreign troublemakers.
The KMP has attacked APEC as a tool of developed countries to promote their economic interests at the expense of less advanced member economies.
The peasants' meeting is one of several events being organised by non-government groups to coincide with the APEC summit.
